references.text: The accusers had already in Luke 23:2 raised the charge that Jesus was stirring up the people. In verse 5, they further strengthen this accusation.
Jesus' ministry began in Galilee, as the accusers point out. Luke 4:14–15 tells us that Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit and taught in the synagogues.
Luke 4:44 confirms that Jesus preached in the synagogues throughout Judea, which aligns with the accusation that he taught 'throughout all Judea'.
Acts 10:37 summarizes Jesus' ministry as beginning in Galilee and spreading throughout Judea, showing a similar geographical pattern to the charge in this verse.
Later, Pilatus refers back to this charge of stirring up the people in Luke 23:14, but he clears Jesus of it.
The parallel account in Mark 15:3 also describes how the chief priests brought many charges against Jesus before Pilate.
In Matthew 27:12, it is also described how the chief priests and elders accused Jesus, paralleling Luke's account.
Luke 7:17 shows that the report about Jesus spread throughout Judea and the surrounding country, supporting the accusation that his teaching reached the entire region.
John 19:12 illustrates a similar tactic where the Jews pressured Pilate by portraying Jesus as a political threat – one who makes himself king sets himself against the emperor.
John 7:1 tells us that Jesus moved about in Galilee because the Jews in Judea were seeking to kill him, showing the ongoing hostility that culminated in the charges in Luke 23.
